title: Clear dry leaves from a gutter
instruction: Scoop the leaves out of the gutter into the blue bucket. Leave the gutter clear and the bucket upright.
context: A gutter scoop must pass beneath the roof overhang and work inside the curved channel without scattering the debris.
setup: A 600 mm length of 112 mm half-round PVC gutter is secured to a timber fascia on a 747.5 mm-high table. Its rim is 140 mm above the table; a roof edge overhangs the opening by 16 mm and a bracket crosses it 220 mm from the centre. Three intact dried bay leaves, 50–70 × 20–30 mm with a shallow natural curl of 4–10 mm lie in the channel. A plastic gutter scoop has a 90 × 110 mm curved bowl and a 140 × 28 × 20 mm hollow handle raised 70 mm above its floor. An empty blue plastic bucket has a 170 mm inner diameter and is 150 mm high. Gutter centre: (300, 0) mm; scoop: (180, 20) mm; bucket: (360, −400) mm. The setup image and geometry specify leaf placement. No leaves are glued or attached.
scoring: After both hands release for one second, score the number of whole leaves entirely inside the bucket divided by 3. The bucket must stay within 40 mm of its starting centre and within 18.2° of upright. Any leaf falling off the work surface or broken equipment makes the score zero. Leaves remaining in the gutter, scoop or on the table earn no credit. Other outcomes score zero. Count leaves from the final views and use a ruler for bucket displacement.
fidelity: Dry leaves use four connected passive panels each, with contact and bending. Mass (0.3 g each) and stiffness are estimates, not measurements of a named packet. No wet adhesion or brittle fragmentation is modelled. The roof section is full size and lowered to a bench-safe height, preserving overhang and bracket access. Native contacts move the scoop and leaves.
scores: Development only: not validated; do not submit.
reset_notes: Use intact dried cooking bay leaves from one packet, at room temperature and kept dry. Choose three within the stated size/curl ranges; no soaking, glue or artificial stiffening. Reuse intact leaves and replace broken ones. Empty the bucket and restore the photographed cluster; allow a few minutes, an estimate rather than a timed test. The secured roof section is reusable and tests local tool access, not ladder use.
